title: A Voice Memo About the Man Who Cut the Line
script: Narrator: [tired] Voice memo to myself, Tuesday evening. I want to remember what happened today at the pharmacy, because I am still thinking about it.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I was waiting in line for almost twenty minutes, because the pharmacist was slow and there were many customers before me.
Narrator: [annoyed] Then a man walked straight to the front and started talking to the pharmacist, as if the line did not exist at all.
Narrator: [honestly] My first feeling was anger. I wanted to shout at him, because I had been standing there so patiently.
Narrator: [reflective] But before I said anything, an older woman behind me spoke calmly. She said, excuse me sir, we have all been waiting, so please join the line.
Narrator: [surprised] The man looked embarrassed. He apologized quietly and walked to the back of the line without arguing further.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I was impressed, because the woman did not shout or insult him. She simply reminded him of what was fair, in a calm and steady voice.
Narrator: [reflective] Later, while I was walking home, I thought about how she handled it, and I realized something important about adab.
Narrator: [warmly] Adab is not only about staying silent when someone is wrong. Sometimes real respect means speaking up, but doing it calmly and kindly.
Narrator: [honestly] If I had shouted instead, the situation would have become worse, and everyone in the pharmacy would have felt uncomfortable and tense.
Narrator: [determined] Next time something like this happens, I want to remember her voice, calm but firm, not angry and not silent either.
Narrator: [gently] I think good manners are sometimes braver than staying quiet, because you have to care enough to say something, while staying kind while doing it.
Narrator: [warmly] So that is my note to myself tonight. Speak calmly, even when you feel frustrated, because how you say something matters just as much as what you say.
Narrator: [peacefully] I hope, next time I am the one who is wrong, someone corrects me with the same patience that woman showed today.

quiz.question: Why was the narrator waiting so long at the pharmacy?
options: The pharmacist was slow and there were many customers
She was chatting with a friend
quiz.explanation: She says she waited almost twenty minutes because the pharmacist was slow and many customers were ahead of her.

quiz.question: What did the man do that upset the narrator?
options: He walked to the front of the line as if it did not exist
He talked loudly on the phone
quiz.explanation: The man walked straight to the front and spoke to the pharmacist, ignoring the line.

quiz.question: What did the older woman say to the man?
options: She asked him to join the line since everyone had been waiting
quiz.explanation: The woman calmly told him everyone had been waiting and asked him to join the line.

quiz.question: How did the man react to the woman's words?
options: He looked embarrassed and went to the back of the line
quiz.explanation: He looked embarrassed, apologized quietly, and walked to the back of the line without arguing.

quiz.question: What lesson does the narrator take from this moment?
options: Speak up calmly and kindly instead of shouting or staying silent
Shouting is the best way to fix problems
quiz.explanation: She concludes that real respect sometimes means speaking up, but doing it calmly, rather than shouting or staying silent.
